text: - Converted Emergency Department wing from electric reheat to hydronic heating. - Upgraded main Emergency Department air handler (AHU-1). - Installed a campus-wide hydronic backbone enabling future electrification. - Integrated the new equipment into our Building Automation System. - Commissioned and balanced all new systems for operational readiness. 5 DE-EE0010150 Benefits Assessment Energy savings are expected through reduced electric reheat usage and optimized chiller performance. The infrastructure supports integration with renewable energy and future electrification projects, reducing long-term carbon emissions. View of the new Roof Top Unit in our Building Automation System: View of the new Chiller Plant in our BAS: 6 DE-EE0010150 Lessons Learned - Supply chain challenges required creative scheduling and patience. - System integration between old and new equipment is challenging, requiring operational adjustments to prioritize patient comfort over maximum efficiency. - Rural hospital electrification is possible when planned around hydronic systems and future-ready equipment. Conclusions The Central Utility Plant Modernization improved efficiency, reliability, and resilience at Klickitat Valley Health. It enables additional decarbonization projects, including a fully designed microgrid (ready for construction despite loss of BRIC funding) and a future ground source heat pump system. The work completed under this grant laid the necessary groundwork for these transformative projects. Future Work/Recommendations - Microgrid: KVH has completed the design of a campus-wide microgrid, initially planned for FEMA BRIC funding. Although federal funding was canceled, the design remains ready for construction when alternative funding is secured. We are using the WA State Climate Commitment Act matching grant to complete the solar carport portion of the microgrid during the summer of 2026. - Ground Source Heat Pump (GSHP): A planned GSHP system will significantly reduce carbon emissions by replacing natural gas heating loads. This project would not be feasible without the hydronic backbone installed under this grant. KVH recently secured 100% funding for the GSHP and will be breaking ground in Q4-2025. Products - Presentations: DOE Energy Storage Grand Challenge Conference (Atlanta), American Healthcare Association Sustainability Summit (panel presentation), KVH Board updates, and regional energy forums. - Media: Ribbon cutting ceremonies with Governor Jay Inslee and Representative Gina Mosbrucker; local newspaper coverage. - StoryMap: https://arcg.is/15Dzfn0 (PNNL project StoryMap).
